gaps.quote: Negation and integer multiplications compose into any fixed rational unit, so multiplying by one, or by its inverse, also costs $O(V)$ (cited)
gaps.note: The page never says how negation is implemented (the paper, line 606-614, fixes block 0 and reverses the other Q-1 blocks, re-reversing bits inside each block), nor that a rational unit is a signed ratio of integers whose numerator and denominator must both be prime to q (paper lines 558-560, 613). The reader cannot check the composition claim from what the page gives.

gaps.quote: The update costs $O(V)$ provided $a$ is computable in $b^{O(1)}$ time
gaps.note: The paper's lemma (lines 561-568) also requires each control used in the offset to have O(b) digits, and the target to follow its controls. The page omits the O(b)-digit hypothesis on the controls, so the stated condition alone is weaker than what the claim needs.
